newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NFI 1 TO BUY TWO FIRMS THIS YEAR.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NFI 1 TO BUY TWO FIRMS THIS YEAR.

text.p: National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 1 in Poland's mass privatisation scheme seeks to buy two firms outside the NFI programme this year, one from the chemical sector, the fund's president said on Monday.
"We're approaching two buy transactions of firms outside the programme. I can say that one of them is in the chemical sector," Zygmunt Makomaski told Reuters.
Makomaski said NFI 1 also sought to sell the strategic stake it holds in eight to 12 of its firms, while it could invest in its other firms along with a strategic partner.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control last year of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international consortia of managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equities in the remaining firms.
Makomaski said another two of the fund's firms would likely soon join on the bourse Lentex and metal pipe maker Huta Ferrum SA, due to enter the main market later this year.

He said up to 12 firms should land on Poland's nascent regulated over-the-counter market, including chemical firm Zaklady Chemiczne Lubon, which sought funds to buy a new production line and boost distribution.
Makomaski said the fund would in most cases take dividends from its firms.
NFI 1 1996 net loss worsened to 46.5 million zlotys from 2.1 million zlotys in 1995.
It made a 5.5-million-zloty net profit in this year's first quarter, but gave no comparison figures.
Under the NFI programme, the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit are entitled from Monday to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund.
The funds, each of which has 31,026,185 shares, are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse as early as mid-June. The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
